satpara-lake.story: Traveller, as you come to Satpara Lake near Skardu in Gilgit-Baltistan, you’ll find a natural lake at 2,600 m above sea level, spanning 4 km² with a picturesque island. It is fed by melting glacial ice from the surrounding mountains and by melting snow from the Deosai Plains, while its only outlet, the Satpara Stream, supplies water to Skardu Valley and drains into the Indus River. Traditional accounts attribute the damming of the lake to the Balti king Ali Senge Anchan, while his queen Mandok Gyalmo took the stream out of it to irrigate her gardens. The completion of Satpara Dam downstream has enlarged the lake, and it provides habitat to the brown and rainbow trout fishes introduced in the region.
satpara-lake.name: Satpara Lake

deosai-national-park.story: Welcome, traveller, to Deosai National Park, a high-elevation national park on an alpine plain between the Skardu District and the Astore District in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan, lying east of Nanga Parbat in the western Himalayas, close to the central Karakoram Range and surrounded by the Deosai Mountains. Here the Deosai Plains sit at an average elevation of 4,114 metres, making them the second highest plateau in the world after the Changtang Tibetan Plateau, and the park protects an area of 843 square kilometres. In spring, this place is covered by sweeps of wildflowers and a wide variety of butterflies. The Balti people call it “Ghbiarsa,” meaning “summer’s place,” because it is only accessible in the summer, while “Deosai” comes from Shina words for “giant” and “shadow,” meaning the “shadow of giant” or the “land of giant.”
deosai-national-park.name: Deosai National Park

sheosar-lake.story: Traveller, if you come to Sheosar Lake, you’ll find an alpine lake at the western end of Deosai National Park, Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan, at 4,250 metres (13,940 ft), regarded as one of the highest altitude lakes in the world. You can reach it by two routes: from Astore, about four hours by jeep through a semi-metal road to Chilum, the last residential area adjacent to the plains, or from Skardu, by jeep in a few hours or by a trek that can take two days. On a clear sunny day, Nanga Parbat peak can be seen from the lake’s location, and while Deosai is snow bound between November and May, spring covers the surrounding area with a wide variety of flowers and butterflies. Most visitors come in summer, between June and early September.
sheosar-lake.name: Sheosar Lake
